sources.title: Richard B. Barnett, Encyclopaedia Iranica: AVADH
sources.note: Original scholarly entry read: eighteenth-century autonomy, 1775 capital, Persian and Urdu, Muharram and annexation. Map interpretation comes from local decoded data.

sources.title: Natalia DiPietrantonio, Metropolitan Museum: Desiring Landscapes, Two Paintings from Avadh, India
sources.note: Direct curator essay read: 1722-1856 Nawabs, Buxar, movement of artists and styles. Does not use speculative sexual interpretation of paintings.

sources.title: NCERT, Themes in Indian History: Rebels and the Raj
sources.note: Original NCERT chapter on IIT Kanpur SATHEE indexed in full; direct access returns 403. Sections on Awadh, subsidiary alliance, taluqdars, peasants and sepoy family connections. Same chapter on SATHEE SSC route treated as one work.

sources.title: British Museum: Ghazi-ud-Din Haidar Shah
sources.note: Original indexed museum biography: nawab 1814-1819, king 1819-1827. These dates take precedence over anomalous medal production range.

sources.title: British Museum: silver coronation medal, 1908,0715.1
sources.note: Direct original object read: portrait and coat of arms with fish, tigers, crown and katar. Object production-date range not used; no inscription transcription supplied by museum.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: A View of the Bara Imambara, 2008.560
sources.note: Direct original object read: circa 1800 view, famine relief, Shia Muharram worship and destroyed gardens/buildings. Exact foundation year not needed.

sources.title: Government of Uttar Pradesh NRI Department: Bara Imambara
sources.note: Direct original government page, About section. Uses labyrinth and stepwell only. Conflicting 1784/1785 dates, night demolition legend and greatest-hall superlative deliberately excluded.

sources.title: LACMA: A Refreshment Stall, M.77.154.2
sources.note: Direct original object description: Lucknow 1750-1775, woman selling fried sweets and tea, figures with vessels. Describes represented scene, not universal dietary practice.

sources.title: LACMA: Perfume Container, M.76.2.27a-L
sources.note: Direct object page: Lucknow circa 1800, silver/enamel, four vials, birds and flowers, perfumed elite hospitality and regional suppliers.

sources.title: Musée Guimet acquisitions report, Arts Asiatiques 60 (2005): MA 12112
sources.note: Direct original museum report, printed page 121, Femmes de haut rang jouant aux échecs, Lucknow 1790-1800. Women, children, eunuchs and attendants; no invented chess rules or universal female literacy.

sources.title: Safura Houshyar, Encyclopaedia Iranica: HAFT QOLZOM
sources.note: Direct original scholarly entry: compilation 1813-1818, Qabul Muhammad, nested seas/springs and grammar. Entry is critical of originality and inherited errors; no claim pioneering lexicography. Catalogue date 1822 pertains to the surviving edition cited separately.

sources.title: Russian State Library / National Electronic Library: Haft Qulzum, Part VII, 1822
sources.note: Direct full original catalogue read and indexed original rechecked: exact Persian title هفت قلزم, Lucknow, His Majesty’s Press, 1822, Persian language and Part VII. Modern catalogue typesetting is the witness used, not visual inspection of a title page; this copy lacks its separate title leaf.

sources.title: Royal Society Library: Haft qulzum = The seven seas, R84202
sources.note: Direct original library catalogue read: romanized title, English parallel title, Lucknow royal press, 1822 and original English title-page details. Combined conservatively with Russian catalogue as the same book work in final checks.

sources.title: La Martiniere College, Lucknow: Infrastructure
sources.note: Original official institutional page indexed in full; direct extraction empty. Reproduced query site:lamartinierelucknow.org/website/about/infrastructure 1845. Uses 1845 school and 1840s wings; no modern classroom facilities backdated.

sources.title: Martin Robert, Medical History 68 (2024): Crafting British medicine in the Empire
sources.note: Direct original scholarly PDF read, printed page 136 / PDF index 8: 1834 royal funding proposal, 350,000 rupees at 4 percent, hospital, proposed Western/Unani teaching and uncertainty about implementation.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture: Begum Hazrat Mahal Moves towards Nepal, 1858
sources.note: Original government text indexed in full, reproducible query site:amritmahotsav.nic.in "Begum Hazrat Mahal Moves" "1858". Direct URL now redirects to new site homepage. Uses regency, March 1858 recapture and retreat, not hagiographic last-breath claim.

proposedOverrides.name: Oudh (Awadh)
proposedOverrides.summary: Awadh’s Lucknow court, rural society and cultural institutions, with British annexation and resistance distinguished from the map’s later cutoff.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Only this exact indexed ID is associated. Awadh aliases checked but absent; no invented identities added.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Eighteenth-century autonomous nawabs, kings from 1819, British annexation 1856 and resistance 1857-1858, followed by colonial context.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Three decoded north Indian polygons. The 1800-1815 shape begins at longitude 81.1286 and omits Lucknow’s capital area; all are approximate and the final polygon persists beyond annexation. Public opening warns of both geography and chronology.
batchIdentityNotes.unresolved: Imported boundary accuracy is not repaired by this narrative. No general household sanitation or universal literacy assertion is made.
